subject: maths
pattern: Linear Programming gives 5-8 marks: 1/2-mark definitions (feasible region, objective function, corner point theorem) and one 5-mark graphical problem, either maximisation or minimisation, from a word problem or direct inequalities. Draw the feasible region, list all corner points, tabulate Z and state the optimum clearly.

questions.q: Define feasible region in a linear programming problem.
questions.answer: The common region determined by all the constraints, including non-negativity restrictions, of an LPP is called the feasible region (solution region). Every point in it is a feasible solution.

questions.q: What is an objective function in an LPP?
questions.answer: The linear function $Z=ax+by$ which is to be maximised or minimised, subject to the given constraints, is called the objective function.

Let $R$ be the feasible region (convex polygon) and $Z=ax+by$ the objective function. If $R$ is bounded, then $Z$ has both a maximum and a minimum value on $R$, and each occurs at a corner point (vertex) of $R$.

questions.q: What are a feasible solution and an infeasible solution?
questions.answer: Any point in the feasible region satisfying all constraints and non-negativity conditions is a feasible solution. Any point that violates at least one constraint (lying outside the feasible region) is an infeasible solution.
Feasible region is the triangle with corner points $(0,0)$, $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$. $Z=0$, $12$, $16$ respectively. Maximum value of $Z$ is $16$ at $(0,4)$.

questions.q: Distinguish between a bounded and an unbounded feasible region.
questions.answer: A feasible region that can be enclosed within a circle is bounded; it always has both maximum and minimum values of $Z$. A region that extends indefinitely in some direction is unbounded; a maximum or minimum may not exist, so one checks whether the open half-plane $Z<m$ (or $Z>M$) has a common point with the region.

Corner points: $(0,0)$, $(2,0)$, $(0,3)$ and the intersection $\left(\frac{20}{19},\frac{45}{19}\right)$. $Z=0,\ 10,\ 9,\ \frac{235}{19}$. Maximum $Z=\frac{235}{19}$ at $\left(\frac{20}{19},\frac{45}{19}\right)$.

questions.q: Explain the steps in solving an LPP by the graphical (corner point) method.
questions.answer: 1) Convert the problem to mathematical form: objective function and constraints. 2) Draw the lines of the constraints and shade the feasible region. 3) Find the coordinates of all corner points. 4) Evaluate $Z$ at each corner point. 5) The largest value is the maximum and the smallest is the minimum. For an unbounded region, check the half-plane $Z>M$ or $Z<m$ for common points.

questions.q: A furniture dealer has Rs 50000 to invest and space for at most 60 pieces. A table costs Rs 2500 and a chair Rs 500; profit is Rs 250 per table and Rs 75 per chair. Formulate and solve graphically to maximise profit.
questions.answer: Let $x$ tables, $y$ chairs. Maximise $Z=250x+75y$ subject to $x+y\le60$, $2500x+500y\le50000\ (5x+y\le100)$, $x,y\ge0$. Corner points: $(0,0)$, $(20,0)$, $(10,50)$, $(0,60)$. $Z=0,\ 5000,\ 6250,\ 4500$. Maximum profit is Rs 6250 with 10 tables and 50 chairs. [Sketch: feasible region quadrilateral O(0,0), (20,0), (10,50), (0,60).]

The feasible region is unbounded with corner points $(0,2)$, $\left(\frac32,\frac12\right)$ (intersection of $x+3y=3$ and $x+y=2$) and $(3,0)$. $Z=10,\ 7,\ 9$. Smallest value $m=7$. Check the half-plane $3x+5y<7$: it has no point in common with the feasible region. Hence the minimum value of $Z$ is $7$ at $\left(\frac32,\frac12\right)$.
